status_summary: No State Department action revoking or narrowing C-175 delegations to other agencies was found. DHS has continued to be a party to international arrangements: its Federal Register notices publish asylum cooperative agreements with Honduras (signed 2025-03-10, with an amendment by notes exchanged 2025-06-25) and a memorandum with Paraguay (signed 2025-08-14). Those notices do not state the legal authority under which they were negotiated, so they do not show whether C-175 authority was revoked, retained or newly granted. The immigration agreements themselves are covered in c05-03. Separately, the State Department published Delegation of Authority No. 620 on 2026-07-02 (91 FR 40651, signed 2026-06-25), which delegates the Secretary's authority to negotiate, conclude and terminate international agreements to the Deputy Secretaries and six Under Secretaries and revokes a 2008 delegation; it cites the Circular 175 procedure as the framework and does not revoke or amend it, so it is not counted as narrowing C-175 authorities.

timeline.event: A DHS, State and Paraguayan agency memorandum on asylum cooperation was signed at Washington, later published by DHS in the Federal Register; the notice does not state the authority basis.

State Department publishes Delegation of Authority No. 620 (91 FR 40651, signed 2026-06-25) delegating the Secretary's treaty and agreement negotiation authority to the Deputy Secretaries and six Under Secretaries and revoking Delegation 311 of 2008; it operates under the Circular 175 procedure, does not amend it and does not narrow other agencies' own authority, though listed officials may authorize other officials to negotiate.
